key_insight: OpenBrain makes AI-generated brain MRI labels easier to audit before reuse. It organizes 35,838 provenance-verified T1-weighted MRI cases from 607 OpenNeuro datasets into confidence-aware case records rather than standalone segmentation files.
problem_solved: Large-scale generated MRI label releases often lack clear evidence about which cases are reliable enough for downstream research.
method: Assemble provenance-verified T1-weighted MRI cases from 607 OpenNeuro source datasets.
Organize each case as an auditable record linking a primary whole-brain parcellation with two committee parcellations.
Structure the release around confidence-aware reuse; the provided abstract does not specify how confidence is calculated.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, OpenBrain could support more traceable selection of generated labels for training and evaluation. Its record-based design provides a basis for inspecting label reliability instead of treating every segmentation as equally trustworthy.
visual_elements: Scale graphic highlighting 35,838 MRI cases across 607 source datasets.
Case-record diagram linking source provenance, a primary parcellation, and two committee parcellations.
Side-by-side brain maps illustrating the primary and committee outputs.
Workflow diagram: OpenNeuro MRI → generated parcellations → auditable case record → downstream reuse.
paper_title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
paper_authors: Qizhen Lan, Yu-Chun Hsu, Yuxiang Wei, Lijing Zhu, Zenan Sun
